newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals mostly up on yen's slip.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals mostly up on yen's slip.

text.p: Tokyo precious metal futures, with the exception of silver, ended mostly firmer on Wednesday, backed by the yen's slide against the dollar, traders said. Trading was nervous amid the volatile currency market.
The newly listed March gold contract ended flat at 1,382 yen. Other prices ranged from one to five yen per gram firmer, with most-active benchmark December ending up one yen at 1,365.

In Tokyo gold futures, individual investors continued to sell futures, taking advantage of the recent price gains to take profits, while trade houses bought futures and sold spot gold in arbitrage dealing.
In the bullion market, spot gold extended its losses from the New York close and was quoted at 351.50/80 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against the New York close of $352.90/353.40.

"Private investors, who still hold massive long positions in gold futures, are expected to continue to unleash their longs," one trader said. Despite a growing perception that the dollar will climb further against the yen, the bearish bullion market limited fresh buying interest at TOCOM.
The focus was the options expiry in New York later today.
"Spot gold may probe the downside at $350 per ounce after the options expiry," another trader said.
Silver prices ended mixed after sharp rises on Tuesday. Benchmark December silver was up 1.3 yen per 10 grams at 193.7 yen.
Most platinum futures contracts rebounded from early lows, as the narrowing gold/platinum spread stimulated short-covering ahead of the close.

Palladium ended firmer. "Sentiment in the palladium market remains bullish due to uncertainty in Japan-Russia platinum group export talks," one trader said. Benchmark December palladium hit its life-of-contract high of 473 yen per gram at the close. --K.Takagi, Tokyo Commodity Desk, +81-3-3432-7431
